title: Understanding Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The bias-variance decomposition is a way to understand the error in a model's predictions. It breaks down the error into three components: the variance of the noise, the bias of the model, and the variance of the model's predictions.

title: Conditions for Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The decomposition holds under certain conditions, such as when the model is trained on data with a known underlying function and noise is independent and identically distributed.

title: Classification Decision Trees and Zero-One Loss
text: Consider how classification decision trees work and how zero-one loss is calculated. Does the bias-variance decomposition apply in this context?

title: Analyzing Zero-One Loss
text: Zero-one loss is a binary loss function that assigns a loss of $$1$$ for incorrect predictions and $$0$$ for correct predictions. How does this affect the bias-variance decomposition?
